CHIEF COMPLAINT
Shortness of breath

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
62-year-old male with type 1 diabetes, congestive heart failure, depression, and reflux presents with shortness of breath for approximately 10 days. Patient reports noticing some swelling and attributes it to recent dietary indiscretion with salty foods at house parties. Reports feeling lethargic. Shortness of breath is exertional, notably with walking up stairs. Patient reports mild leg swelling. Denies difficulty lying flat but reports morning stiffness and discomfort upon waking that takes time to resolve. Reports one episode of acute shortness of breath at night approximately one week ago that has not recurred. Blood sugars have been well-controlled on insulin pump; patient monitors during weekdays but occasionally forgets on weekends. Denies recent spike in blood glucose. Depression has been present over the past year and a half; patient has been trying natural solutions including outdoor stretching in summer but acknowledges difficulty with weather changes and is not yet ready to try medications. Patient reports difficulty with alcohol during holiday season but improving. Reflux well-controlled on omeprazole with lifestyle modifications including reduction of Red Bull and caffeine. Denies suicidal or homicidal ideation.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorsed shortness of breath on review of systems sheet completed at check-in. Denies chest pain, fever, chills, cough, or abdominal pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 1 diabetes
Congestive heart failure
Depression
Reflux

MEDICATIONS
Insulin pump
Omeprazole 20 milligrams daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports affinity for chocolate bars. Acknowledges dietary indiscretion with salty foods. Alcohol use increased during holidays but improving. Works during the week and busy on weekends.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Pulse oximetry normal. Neck exam: No jugular venous distension, no carotid bruits. Cardiac exam: 3 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated. Lung exam: Crackles bilaterally at bases. Lower extremity exam: 1+ pitting edema.

RESULTS
Chest X-ray: No evidence of airspace disease. Labs: White blood cell count not elevated, no evidence of infection or pneumonia.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Shortness of breath/Acute heart failure exacerbation: Start lasix 40 milligrams daily. Patient to weigh himself daily and call if weight not decreasing or if increasing. Patient instructed to call or go to emergency room if shortness of breath worsens at rest, as may need intravenous diuretics.
2. Type 1 diabetes: Order hemoglobin A1c in approximately one month to assess for needed adjustments. Patient to follow up with endocrinologist. Ensure recent eye exam completed.
3. Depression: Refer to psychiatry for talk therapy. No medications at this time.
4. Reflux: Continue omeprazole 20 milligrams daily.
